$comment: Canonical list of PrayerKey identifiers — stable, language-independent keys for every fixed prayer text, each translated into all 6 languages (see ARCHITECTURE.md#content-layer). Source of truth: iOS's Mocks/Content/PrayerKey.swift (camelCase cases here); Android's content/PrayerKey.kt and Windows's Localization/PrayerKey.cs (PascalCase consts) must carry the exact same set. Keep in sync whenever a key is added, removed, or its purpose changes on any platform — see README.md in this directory.

keys.note: Not currently used in the Rosary flow itself; kept for future use (Mass responses, other prayers).

keys.text: Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord

keys.note: The oldest known Marian prayer; traditionally recited on its own, without a versicle/collect.
Reused verbatim for the Angelus's Eastertide/Regina Caeli substitution.

keys.text: Hail Mary — for an increase of Faith
keys.note: The opening Hail Mary, first of three.

keys.text: Hail Mary — for an increase of Hope
Hail Mary — for an increase of Charity

keys.note: Distinct from versiculumStandard (the Rosary's) and versiculumPaschale (reused for the Angelus's Eastertide substitution).

keys.text: Jesus Prayer ("Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner.")
Stations of the Cross — opening act of contrition (adapted from St. Alphonsus Liguori)
Stations of the Cross — V. ("We adore You, O Christ..."), repeated before each of the 14 stations
Stations of the Cross — R. ("...redeemed the world"), repeated before each of the 14 stations
Stations of the Cross — closing prayer
Seven Sorrows — V. ("Pray for us, O most sorrowful Virgin"), prayed once after the 3 closing Hail Marys
Seven Sorrows — R. ("...worthy of the promises of Christ"), prayed once after the 3 closing Hail Marys
Seven Sorrows — closing collect (the traditional Septem Dolorum B.M.V. prayer, "O God, in whose Passion...")
Divine Mercy Chaplet — the Our-Father-bead offering ("Eternal Father, I offer You..."), repeated identically at the start of all 5 decades
Divine Mercy Chaplet — the Hail-Mary-bead petition ("For the sake of His sorrowful Passion..."), repeated identically ×10 in all 5 decades
Divine Mercy Chaplet — closing acclamation ("Holy God, Holy Mighty One, Holy Immortal One..."), prayed 3 times after the 5th decade
